title: Log an adaptation's changed facts
statement: When an adaptation changes a fact of the original, such as a count, record the change, keep it consistent everywhere, and never assess it as true of the original.
example: One retelling's changed count of four losses was repeated in a reveal, a later lesson's frame and a chart.
detail: A source audit of a Grade 4 retelling found that it changed how many companions went and how many were lost, with no adaptation change register attached to the student passage. The changed count was reinforced in feedback, a reveal, later lesson frames and a chart, and the lesson's own assessment grounding contradicted the passage about who was counted. The audit asked that any count changed for adaptation be logged and never presented as a fact about the original, and that the contradictory grounding be resolved in any case.

evidence.quote: If loss counts are changed for adaptation, log the decision and never present that count as a fact about the original epic; resolve the contradictory grounding in any case.
The p17 reveal at `:3196`, L3 p16 frame at `:4559` and p18 chart at `:4723` reinforce four losses.

Retelling status is explicit in the plan; no exact translator, edition, source passage or adaptation change register is attached to the student passage. Changes the party/loss counts and carries them into graded work.
Numeric alterations are reinforced in feedback and later L3 frames.
